title: Late Breaking Results: Opera: An Open and Efficient Platform for Data-driven Synthesis of Analog Circuits
problem: Analog circuit synthesis is data-driven but bottlenecked by expensive circuit simulators in the synthesis loop; benchmarking methods requires exclusive access to commercial semiconductor technology.
method: Opera develops efficient surrogate models (neural networks) to replace expensive SPICE simulators; integrates surrogate models into OpenAI Gym-like environments for optimization; built on open-source 45nm semiconductor process for reproducibility.

title: Physical Synthesis Optimization Prediction Using Machine Learning
problem: Long EDA tool runtimes act as bottlenecks for design turn-around-time in complex SOC design implementation, requiring designers to wait for complete tool runs to obtain critical Power-Performance-Area (PPA) parameters such as timing slack, critical path depth, leakage power, and area.
method: Supervised machine learning model trained on rich sub-10nm SOC design implementation datasets to predict PPA component data early in the physical synthesis flow. Training leverages actual tool run outcomes from a variety of design scenarios at typical 1 GHz clock speeds.

title: Advancing Functional Safety: Improving Failure Mode Analysis and Fault Injection Using Automation and GNN Algorithms
problem: Complex electronic systems require Failure Mode Analysis and Fault Injection for functional safety, but traditional methods suffer from high simulation time, manual effort, and scalability challenges.
method: Two-part solution: (1) FMA automation system ensuring consistency and reducing manual effort, (2) GNN-based acceleration of FI process using GCNII model to detect critical nodes and predict fault criticality.

title: Plexus: Taming Billion-edge Graphs with 3D Parallel Full-graph GNN Training
problem: Graph neural networks (GNNs) on large real-world graphs with billions of edges exceed GPU memory capacity. Distributed full-graph training suffers from high communication overhead and load imbalance due to irregular graph structure. Mini-batch sampling approaches sacrifice model quality.
method: Three-dimensional (3D) parallel approach for full-graph GNN training combining spatial and temporal parallelism. Double permutation scheme for load balancing addresses irregular graph structure. Performance model predicts optimal 3D configuration automatically. Evaluated on six graph datasets across up to 2048 GPUs (Perlmutter) and 1024 GPUs (Frontier).

title: PAF-Enc: Position Affine Encoding to Reduce Bit-Flips in Non-Volatile Main Memories
problem: Emerging non-volatile memories (NVMs) used as main memory suffer from reduced lifetime and performance due to high write operations. Bit disparity between stored and incoming data creates unnecessary write operations, accelerating wear and limiting system lifespan.
method: Two-stage position-affine encoding (PAF-Enc) technique: (1) analyze memory data patterns to generate affine masks; (2) encode incoming cache blocks using XOR operations with masks to maximize resemblance to stored data before write, reducing bit disparity and write operations.

title: BMC Engine Sequencing with Graph Neural Network Embeddings of Hardware Circuits
problem: Formal verification via Bounded Model Checking (BMC) requires engine selection and sequencing; traditional approaches lack intelligent switching between engines at different verification depths.
method: Use GNN embeddings of hardware circuits (via DeepGate2 tool) to drive BMC engine selection strategy. Learns to switch between engines at different depths based on circuit structure.

title: HPC-R1: Characterizing R1-like Large Reasoning Models on HPC
problem: Limited understanding of Large Reasoning Model (LRM) training performance and system inefficiencies on HPC systems; complex multi-stage workflows challenging to optimize.
method: HPC-R1: characterization of LRM training stages (SFT, GRPO-based RL, generation, distillation) on NERSC Perlmutter; detailed performance analysis.

title: Diff-MoE: Efficient Batched MoE Inference with Priority-Driven Differential Expert Caching
problem: MoE models require massive expert parameter storage; existing GPU memory management solutions use sophisticated prefetching but suffer communication bottlenecks at large batch sizes
method: Differential cache hierarchy: globally-hot experts in high-priority per-layer caches, locally-hot in medium-priority caches under LRU with predictive prefetch, cold experts cached on-demand

title: Exploiting Power Side-Channel Vulnerabilities in XGBoost Accelerator
problem: XGBoost accelerators on FPGAs are vulnerable to power side-channel attacks that can leak sensitive model data and enable model extraction.
method: Demonstrates power side-channel attacks by analyzing power consumption variations to infer XGBoost decision tree node features; uses empirical testing on Sakura-X platform with FAXID accelerator to deduce model decisions.

title: Enabling On-Tiny-Device Model Personalization via Gradient Condensing and Alternant Partial Update
problem: On-device training and model personalization on tiny embedded devices (e.g., <1 MB SRAM, 2 MB Flash); multi-layer backpropagation incurs prohibitive computational and memory cost on resource-constrained devices.
method: Algorithm-system co-optimization framework TinyMP: (1) Gradient Condensing reduces gradient map structure complexity and memory consumption while preserving model performance; (2) Alternant Partial Update locally and alternatively selects essential parameters to update without retraining or offline evolutionary search, reducing computation overhead.

title: Microscopic-Level Mouse Whole Cortex Simulation Composed of 9 Million Biophysical Neurons and 26 Billion Synapses on the Supercomputer Fugaku
problem: Understanding brain structure and function at cellular/synaptic level; simulating biophysical neural models at whole-cortex scale requires extreme computational resources
method: Lightweight biophysical neuron simulator optimized for Fugaku supercomputer; strong scaling benchmark up to 152,064 compute nodes; whole mouse cerebral cortex simulation on 145,728 Fugaku nodes

title: Reproducibility Report for SC25 Paper Optimizing Quantum Circuit Mapping to Reduce Inter-Module Communications in Distributed Architectures
problem: Artifact evaluation and reproducibility assessment for quantum circuit mapping optimization work.
method: Artifact evaluation as part of SC25 Reproducibility Initiative. Reviewer conducted evaluation of artifact description and evaluation appendix.

title: 9.2 A 400MHz Symbol-Power-Tracking (SPT) Supply Modulator with SPT-Adaptive-Biasing Network Supporting 5G FR2 CMOS PA
problem: 5G NR FR2 (mmWave) power amplifiers suffer from high peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR) in OFDM with complex modulations (QAM), causing substantial power consumption at average levels. Envelope tracking (ET) improves efficiency at power back-off but is limited to ~200MHz bandwidth; digital envelope tracking and symbol power tracking (SPT) can exceed this but require robust supply modulation.
method: A 400MHz symbol-power-tracking (SPT) supply modulator with SPT-adaptive-biasing network supports 5G FR2 CMOS PA. SPT tracks symbol-level power rather than continuous envelope, enabling higher modulation bandwidth. Adaptive biasing adjusts transistor bias in real time to maintain efficiency across varying power levels.

title: LightML: A Photonic Accelerator for Efficient General Purpose Machine Learning
problem: General-purpose machine learning workloads require massive computational throughput that strains conventional electronic server infrastructure in terms of cost and power. Existing photonic computing proposals lack a complete system-level design with proper memory and buffer support to fully utilize the high-speed photonic crossbar.
method: LightML implements the first complete system-level photonic crossbar design for ML, pairing a photonic crossbar core with a carefully co-designed memory and buffer architecture that sustains greater than 80% utilization of the photonic crossbar. The system supports large-scale matrix-matrix multiplication (MMM), element-wise operations, non-linear activation functions, and convolutional layers via dedicated photonic and electronic functional units. The design targets both edge and data-center density profiles, delivering 325 TOP/s at 3 W.

title: HybriMoE: Hybrid CPU-GPU Scheduling and Cache Management for Efficient MoE Inference
problem: MoE inference on resource-constrained hybrid CPU-GPU platforms requires offloading experts, but unstable expert activation patterns and complex workload distribution prevent efficient CPU-GPU scheduling and memory utilization.
method: HybriMoE combines three techniques: (1) dynamic intra-layer scheduling that redistributes workloads between CPU and GPU per layer based on expert activation patterns, (2) impact-driven inter-layer prefetching that predicts required experts, (3) score-based KV/expert caching prioritizing high-value data.

title: Extending THAPI with CXI Hardware Counter Sampling for High Resolution NIC Telemetry
problem: Existing HPC tracing tools lack insight into low-level network interface controller (NIC) behavior; NIC hardware counters revealing congestion and retries remain underutilized despite providing critical performance information
method: Extension of THAPI framework with sampling plugin for CXI (Cassini Interconnect) hardware counters; periodic collection of NIC metrics integrated into HPC trace timelines via iprof tool; visualization in Perfetto showing correlation between network events and application behavior
